state.purpose: This consultation concerns a proposed language direction only. A Can user suspects effortless state-machine authoring is absent. Can targets business apps, economical AI generation, small source, straightforward ownership and reusable declarations. There is no agreed grammar and no request to build a runtime here.
state.observed: In inspected ExpenseFlow source, draft/submitted/approved/rejected are enum values with draft as default. Submission checks claimant and current draft state before setting submitted. Approval checks reviewer access, submitted state and a different claimant, then writes status and decision evidence. Locks express protected and final fields elsewhere. Inspected compiler syntax covers require/set, scenarios/CRUD, event delivery and timers, without an app-machine node. State runtime files implement provisional mutation plus admission and revision-fenced history/receipt/outbox/schedule commit. This inspection does not qualify the whole sample app.
state.requirements: Each candidate must be assessed against legal paths that tools can inspect; typed inputs; normal caller/source authority and domain conditions; protection from alternate writers; transactional status/evidence changes; original check/effect ordering; version conflicts, replay and delayed events; attached behavioral examples; concise and composable authoring. Initialization, upgrades, same-state edges, branch-dependent targets and changed graphs remain specifications to settle. Browser affordances cannot grant authority or reveal protected predicates. Providers keep asynchronous delivery uncertainty.
state.alternatives: Option A retains existing enums and scenarios and adds inferred diagrams, diagnostics and writing guidance. Conditional code may prevent a complete graph, so it does not promise a new enforced language contract. Option B introduces a model-field lifecycle opt-in and declares its edges with the existing operations or trusted handlers, using current compiler/storage owners for checks; comprehensive mutation coverage and evaluation position are obligations. Option C defines a reusable machine type centrally and binds records and operations to it; this offers graph sharing but must avoid copied permission/signature/identity definitions. Flat initial scope is possible for every option, and none inherently requires separate execution infrastructure.
state.boundaries: The reviewed workload has not established demand for nested/parallel/history states, implicit entry/exit actions or immediate cascading transitions. SCXML supplies richer statechart and event-completion semantics; Stately explains guarded event transitions. Omitting those initially restricts capability, and future evidence may change the scope. Select an investigation path rather than declare implementation correctness.

direction.instructions: On the evidence and common acceptance outcomes provided, which approach merits the first Can state-machine design investigation?

criteria.existing: Improve enum-and-scenario conventions and graph inspection first, keeping their acknowledged limitations unless a demonstrated need justifies new syntax.
criteria.model_lifecycle: Explore field-owned lifecycle declarations whose edges come from canonical operations and whose enforcement belongs to the current compiler and commit path.
criteria.machine_type: Explore a shareable named state-machine type with one edge definition and bindings to ordinary operations and record authority.
criteria.defer: Keep the structural choice open because the present examples and outstanding semantic questions are insufficient to prefer an approach.
